observation: Read all3725selected characters. The abstract connects four interacting welfare scores to land-specific weights, policy scenarios, a ranking objective and twenty-year outcomes. Its recommendations preserve differences by land type: preservation-zone restrictions, settlement employment/bridging organizations for most years, and alternative grazing-zone combinations. The temporal qualifier and alternative combinations should survive synthesis instead of one universal policy. Forecast inputs and residual variation precede long-term results; the author later makes broad precision, stability and universality claims whose evidence strength is not assessed here. The last paragraph returns to the human/wildlife balance. Form headings remain, and community- based needs source wrap comparison; printed net-work wording is retained without polishing. No source completeness, ecological/model or figure correctness acceptance.
